entities.summary:
Samuel "Sambo" Mockbee was an American architect and a co-founder of the Auburn University Rural Studio program in Hale County, Alabama. After establishing a regular architectural practice in his native Mississippi, Mockbee became interested in the design and construction problems associated with rural housing in Alabama and Mississippi. Soon after joining the faculty of Auburn, Mockbee established the Rural Studio with educator Dennis K.

Ruth to provide practical training for architecture students in an environment where their efforts could address the problems of poverty and substandard housing in underserved areas of the southern United States. Samuel Mockbee was a architects & engineers from Meridian (1944-12-23, Meridian–2001-12-30). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Samuel Mockbee's work at Auburn University Rural Studio addressed poverty and substandard housing in underserved areas of the southern United States through practical training for architecture students. His efforts led to over 1,000 homes built by students between 1975 and 2002.
